_comment:
The cutout cheat for a spin. A whole actor cannot be rotated, so a revolution is sold by SQUASHING the actor horizontally to an edge-on sliver at the halfway point and popping back out - `parts` on `body` with a small scaleX, which snaps rather than tweens, which is precisely right: a revolution has no in-between frames in limited animation, it has a wide frame, a thin frame and a wide frame. Three revolutions, each thinner-sliver-shallower than the last (0.16 -> 0.20 -> 0.34) so the spin visibly slows down, then a head-thrown-by-momentum wobble and a settle.

Each thin frame is held 0.20-0.22s - well over the 0.17s two-frame floor at 12fps - because a sliver that lands and leaves inside two frames is not a spin, it is a flicker. The anticipation is the 0.4s wind-up LEAN in the opposite direction before anything moves; without it the first squash reads as a rendering glitch.

What it deliberately does NOT animate: any actual rotation, and the arms - there are none guaranteed. Tier 1-3 only, so it casts on every rig.
